newsitem.title: USA: Minn. Twins to consider sale or relocation - owner.
newsitem.headline: Minn. Twins to consider sale or relocation - owner.

text.p: Minnesota Twins owner Carl Pohlad announced Tuesday that he will withdraw any team contribution to a new ballpark and seek formal permission from major league owners to explore other options for the franchise, including relocation.

The failure of Minnesota lawmakers to approve a plan for a new stadium for the team in the recently concluded session, and apparent lack of interest in preparing a plan in the future, left the team no choice, Pohlad said in a statement.
Minnesota lawmakers rejected numerous financing proposals for a new $400 million retractable roof stadium to replace the Twins current facility during the session concluded earlier in May.

The team's lease at the Metrodome runs through 2011, but includes an escape clause the Twins can exercise after the 1998 season if ticket sales are poor in relation to the rest of the league or the ballclub loses money three years in a row.
Minnesota Gov. Arne Carlson, a supporter of proposals to build a new ballpark, is scheduled to meet Wednesday with legislative leaders to discuss the agenda for an upcoming special session.
Thusfar, financing for a new ballpark and a new St. Paul arena are not on the schedule.

The Twins will seek permission to consider a sale in the open market, relocation, sharing the franchise with another market or operating the team strictly within the current operating revenues, Pohlad said.
The team would consider legislative solutions before the end of the 1997 season, but will not wait for a decision in the 1998 legislative session, Pohlad said.

"Since the end of the session the legislature has not provided any cause for optimism or reassurance that this matter will be dealt with in a timely manner," Pohlad said. "The lack of action and the indifference of the legislature forces us to move on."
Pohlad made a similar statement in a letter to lawmakers last week and sought to further clarify his position Tuesday.
